subject: Re: DPA + SCCs + Subprocessor audit scope — final sign-off and e-sign plan
messages:
From: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@medcorps.com>
To: sean_gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@medcorps.com
Date: Mon, 22 Feb 2027 14:05:12 +0000
Subject: DPA redline and audit evidence list

Sean —

Thanks for sending the draft. We reviewed the DPA and have three high-level asks before procurement can route for approval: 

1) Confirmation that Redwood will accept the EU SCCs (we need the executed annex).
2) Narrowing the audit right language — our security team prefers an on-site or remote review by a third-party auditor versus granting broad, customer-initiated audits. Can you confirm Redwood will accept a SOC 2 + shared pen test summary workflow instead of unlimited audit access?
3) Subprocessor list and flow-down: procurement wants an explicit commitment that MedCorps will be notified 30 days prior to onboarding any subprocessors with access to PHI or tokenized data.

I've attached a redline (see MedCorps_DPA_redline_v3.docx) and SOC2/pen test summaries (redacted). Can you confirm Redwood's position on each point and propose final wording for the audit clause? We need to get this signed via e-sign by 3/7 to keep our go-live target.

Best,
Elena
Head of Procurement — MedCorps Health

Attachments: MedCorps_DPA_redline_v3.docx (docx), SOC2-summary-2026-redacted.pdf (pdf), pen-test-summary-redacted.pdf (pdf)
From: sean_gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@medcorps.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Feb 2027 15:02:30 -0500
Subject: Re: DPA redline and audit evidence list

Elena — thanks for the clear asks. Quick responses inline: 

1) SCCs: yes, we will execute the standard EU SCC Addendum as an annex to the DPA. We will deliver the executed annex as part of the DocuSign packet.

2) Audit rights: Redwood prefers the third-party auditor + shared evidence approach for customers — scope limited to customer-specific systems and the period of contract. We can accept language that requires Redwood to provide SOC 2 Type II attestation and a redacted pen test summary annually, and to facilitate a one-time third-party audit under mutually agreed scope and NDAs for situations where additional assurance is justified. We cannot accept unrestricted on-site audit rights.

3) Subprocessors: we already publish a live subprocessor registry; we can commit to 30 days' notice for subprocessors that will process regulated data (e.g., PHI). We'll add a clause to the DPA that new subprocessors handling regulated data will require written notification and an opportunity for objection within 30 days.

I'll loop Grace (legal) and Karthik (privacy) to finalize precise wording. If that matches MedCorps' minimums, we can prepare a final DocuSign envelope by EOD Thursday and target execution by 3/7.

Next steps: Grace will propose final redact-friendly wording on the audit clause; Marissa will coordinate DocuSign routing and signature order.

Thanks — Sean
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@medcorps.com>
Cc: sean_gallagher <sean@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 23 Feb 2027 09:10:45 -0500
Subject: Re: DPA redline and audit evidence list

Hi Elena —

Appreciate the quick read. Proposed language below (excerpt to be inserted into Section 7 — Audit and Verification):

"Redwood shall provide, upon Customer request, the following forms of evidence: (i) the most recent SOC 2 Type II report covering the Services; (ii) a redacted penetration test executive summary assessing controls relevant to the Services; and (iii) reasonable cooperation to facilitate one (1) third-party audit of Customer-specific processing upon mutual written agreement of scope, schedule, and confidentiality terms. Customer-initiated audits beyond the single agreed audit are subject to Redwood's prior approval and may require Customer to bear reasonable costs for on-site activities."

We recommend an NDAs-and-scope clause to protect Redwood's proprietary tooling. Also suggest a carve-out that any audit access to production systems will be via remote sessions or controlled evidence delivery rather than direct hands-on access.

Does MedCorps need explicit language around vulnerability timelines (e.g., disclose critical findings within 7 days)? We can add an SLA for critical vulnerability notifications if needed.

— Grace
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
From: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@medcorps.com>
To: grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, sean_gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@medcorps.com, J. Patel <j.patel@healthops.io>
Date: Wed, 24 Feb 2027 11:23:08 +0000
Subject: Re: DPA redline and audit evidence list

Grace — thanks for the draft language; that's helpful and closer to what we need. A few clarifications from our security governance team: 

• The one-time third-party audit must be able to examine customer-specific configurations, logs (redacted for other customers), and any subprocessor contracts that materially affect data flows.
• Vulnerability disclosure: critical severity — disclosure within 7 calendar days and remediation plan within 30 days.

If Redwood can add a line that states Redwood will provide a redacted copy of any subprocessor SOC 2 or equivalent evidence upon request for those subprocessors processing our regulated data, that will satisfy procurement.

Assuming the redline includes these points, procurement is prepared to proceed to signature via DocuSign. Please confirm and include an updated redline that we can upload into our contract system.

Regards,
Elena
From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@medcorps.com>
Cc: sean_gallagher <sean@redwood.com>, grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Feb 2027 16:02:00 +0000
Subject: Final DPA redline and DocuSign packet ready for signature

Elena — quick update from our side. Attached is an updated redline that incorporates Grace's audit clause language with two additions per your ask: (a) explicit commitment to provide redacted subprocessor SOC 2 evidence on request for subprocessors handling regulated data; (b) a vulnerability disclosure SLA for critical findings (7 days disclosure, 30 days remediation plan).

We've prepared the DocuSign envelope with the following sign order: (1) MedCorps procurement lead; (2) MedCorps legal; (3) Redwood legal (Grace); (4) Redwood accounts exec (Sean). DocuSign link: https://www.docusign.com/en/link/abc123-dpa-sign.

Attachments in envelope: MedCorps_DPA_redline_v3.docx, SOC2-summary-2026-redacted.pdf, pen-test-summary-redacted.pdf.

Please let us know if the procurement lead needs any additional credentials or if you'd like to schedule a 15-minute call to walk through the audit clause. Goal: E-signed DPA by 03/07 to keep the onboarding timeline intact.

Thanks all —
Marissa
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
